answer_1.quote: Automatic text simplification (ATS) is the task of reducing the complexity of a text without changing its original content and meaning.

answer_2.quote: For automatic evaluation, we use SARI, the average of the F1 score for adding, keeping, and deleting n-grams (n ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}). SARI has been shown to correlate with human judgments of simplicity. We also report BLEU, a common metric in machine translation.

answer_4.quote: For manual evaluation, we enlisted eight volunteers to annotate system outputs in English, Russian, Italian, and Urdu (two in each language) for three properties: Adequacy (is the meaning preserved?), Fluency (is the simplification eloquent/grammatical?), and Simplicity (is the output simpler?).
answer_4.guideline: Adequacy (is the meaning preserved?), Fluency (is the simplification eloquent/grammatical?), and Simplicity (is the output simpler?)
